key rationale.Nitroglycerin if indicated: For ongoing ischemic chest pain if no hypotension/right-ventricular infarct concern.
key rationale.Cath lab / Admit: STEMI → activate PCI. Unstable → monitored bed.

key rationale.Thiamine IV: Before dextrose in malnourished / alcoholic patients.
key rationale.CT Head non-contrast: Rule out bleed before tPA or if trauma concern.
key rationale.Focused Neurologic Exam: Rapid neuro exam helps localize deficits and guides immediate imaging urgency.
key rationale.Chest X-ray: Helps identify aspiration or pulmonary source when infection is suspected.
key rationale.Toxicology Screen: Supports overdose/metabolic differential when presentation is unclear.
key rationale.Monitor / ICU admit: Protect airway if GCS falling; continuous neuro checks.

key rationale.Abdominal Exam: Targeted abdominal exam helps localize pain and peritoneal signs.
key rationale.Pelvic Exam: Speculum/bimanual exam helps detect tenderness, discharge, or cervical motion pain.
key rationale.STD Screening: NAAT and related labs help identify infectious causes of pelvic pain.
key rationale.IV Access + Type & Screen: Two large-bore if unstable or rupture concern.

key rationale.CBC \u00b7 Lipase \u00b7 LFTs \u00b7 UA: Narrow differential: biliary, pancreatic, UTI, medical.
key rationale.CT Abdomen/Pelvis: High yield for appendicitis, diverticulitis, obstruction.
key rationale.Antibiotics if indicated: Give before OR if sepsis or perforation suspected.

key rationale.CT Head: Non-contrast first for thunderclap or neuro deficit.
key rationale.BP Management: Treat only if hypertensive emergency criteria met.
key rationale.MRI / MRA if indicated: Venous sinus thrombosis, posterior fossa lesions.
key rationale.Observation / Neuro: Worst headache of life → admit until SAH excluded.

correct orders: BMP · CBC · TSH · B12 · RPR · Tox screen

key rationale.Cardiac Monitor + Continuous vitals: Track hemodynamics and oxygenation while evaluating AMS or acute cognitive change.
key rationale.IV Access + fluids: Resuscitate and allow medication administration during the workup.
key rationale.Point-of-care Glucose: Hypoglycemia mimics stroke and acute confusion — treat immediately if low.
key rationale.Focused Neurologic & Mental Status Exam: Document orientation, memory, language, and focal deficits to guide urgency.
key rationale.CT Head non-contrast: Rule out hemorrhage, mass effect, or acute structural lesion.
key rationale.BMP \u00b7 CBC \u00b7 TSH \u00b7 B12 \u0: Metabolic, infectious, endocrine, nutritional, and toxic causes of memory change.
key rationale.MRI Brain / Neuroimaging: Higher yield for subacute stroke, encephalitis, and structural lesions when CT is unrevealing.
key rationale.Neurology Consult + Admit: Progressive or unexplained cognitive decline needs inpatient evaluation and safety planning.

key rationale.Empiric Antibiotics IV: Do not delay for LP if unstable or petechial rash.
key rationale.IV Fluid Bolus: Septic shock physiology common in toxic presentations.
key rationale.Blood Cultures: Before antibiotics when possible — not if delaying care.

key rationale.MRI Spine if cord signs: Cord compression is a surgical emergency.
key rationale.Admit / Neuro consult: Progressive weakness or respiratory concern → ICU.

key rationale.Urinalysis + Culture: Culture guides therapy; send before antibiotics if stable.
key rationale.Empiric Antibiotics: Cover E. coli; adjust for local resistance.
key rationale.Urology / Admit: Male with fever, obstruction, or sepsis.

key rationale.Oxygen / BIPAP: Target SpO₂ per protocol; prepare intubation if tiring.
key rationale.BNP \u00b7 D-dimer \u00b7 ABG: PE workup, CHF, CO₂ retention in COPD.
key rationale.CT Pulmonary Angiography: If PE suspected and pre-test probability warrants.
key rationale.ICU if unstable: BiPAP failure, shock, or rising work of breathing.

key rationale.Cardiac Monitor + Pulse ox: Continuous vitals in a potentially septic infant.
key rationale.Stat Labs (CBC, BMP, glucose): Screen for dehydration, infection, and metabolic derangement.
key rationale.Blood Culture: Obtain before antibiotics in febrile infant workup.
key rationale.Urinalysis + Culture: UTI is a common occult source in poor feeding and fever.
key rationale.Chest X-ray: Evaluate respiratory source if tachypneic or hypoxic.
key rationale.Antipyretic + Comfort care: Treat fever while avoiding premature closure on sepsis.
key rationale.Admit / Observation: High-risk infant needs monitored workup and serial exams.
